description: Unique synthetic transaction ID (chronological order).
Synthetic transaction date and time (2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31).
Fully synthetic sender VPA. Not a real UPI ID. Exclude from model features.
Fully synthetic recipient VPA (opaque; prefix does not reveal type). Exclude from model features: mule IDs repeat.
Transaction amount in INR; capped at Rs 1,00,000 (typical UPI per-transaction limit).
Hour of transaction (0-23).
Day of week, Monday = 0.
1 if Saturday/Sunday.
1 if transaction between 23:00 and 05:59.
Sender age band (scams target different groups with different probability).
Sender city tier.
Age of the sender's UPI registration in days.
Sender's average transaction amount over the previous 30 days (INR).
amount_inr / sender_avg_amount_30d; spikes indicate out-of-pattern payments.
Sender's transactions in the 24 h before this one (simulated).
Sender's transactions in the 7 days before this one (>= 24 h count).
Recipient account type as registered (some fake 'merchants' exist).
Age of recipient account in days; very new accounts are riskier but not always fraudulent.
Recipient reputation (0 = worst, 100 = best) from simulated network/complaint history.
Number of prior complaints against the recipient (many mule accounts have 0).
Distinct senders paying this recipient in last 24 h incl. this one (fan-in).
Earlier payments from this sender to this recipient.
1 if prior_txns_with_recipient == 0.
Declared/inferred payment purpose. Includes legit and scam-style purposes; legit rows can carry scam-style purposes.
How the payment was initiated.
values_or_range: QR_Scan, UPI_ID_Manual, Collect_Request, Contact_Pick, Payment_Link, Merchant_Intent

description: QR code scanned to pay (payment_channel == QR_Scan).
Payment initiated by approving a collect request.
QR payee name/type does not match the claimed merchant or purpose (only possible when is_qr_payment = 1).
Collect request the sender did not expect (only possible when is_collect_request = 1).
Sender was pressured to pay immediately or within a deadline (legit bills can be urgent too).
Payment framed as a refund, cashback, prize or reward claim.
Recipient/contact claims to be a bank, company, official, relative or boss (system flag; has false positives).
Sender was asked to enter UPI PIN to 'receive' money (PIN is only ever needed to send).
Payment arrived through a link flagged suspicious (shortened, unknown domain, phishing-like).
Sender was asked to install/use a screen-sharing or remote-access app.
Recipient name verification result.
Social engineering: contact claims to be police, CBI, RBI, TRAI, bank or customs.
Social engineering: interaction initiated by the other party (call/SMS/message).
Social engineering: sender told not to tell family/bank/anyone.
Social engineering: fear, threat, greed or emotional manipulation present.
Sender was on a phone/video call while making the payment.
Composite 0-1 social-engineering score from the five indicators above + urgency + impersonation, with noise. Derived from features only.
TARGET (binary): 1 = fraudulent transaction.
TARGET (multiclass): scam type, or 'Legitimate'. Never use as a feature for is_fraud.
TARGET (ordinal): analyst-style triage level. Derived from a rule score + outcome; never use as a feature for is_fraud.
